title: Depression in adults: treatment and management
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
journal: NICE guideline NG222, published 29 June 2022; recommendations 1.5 and 1.6, tables 1 and 2
funder: not stated in the guideline text.
result: Treatment options for a new episode of less severe depression (PHQ-9 below 16), in order of the committee's interpretation of clinical and cost effectiveness and implementation: guided self-help, group CBT, group behavioural activation, individual CBT, individual behavioural activation, group exercise (moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, usually more than one session a week for 10 weeks), group mindfulness and meditation, interpersonal psychotherapy, SSRIs, counselling, short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy; antidepressants are not routinely offered first-line for less severe depression unless that is the person's informed preference. For more severe depression, all options in table 2 can be first-line, in the order: individual CBT combined with an antidepressant, individual CBT, individual behavioural activation, antidepressant medication, individual problem-solving, counselling, short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy, interpersonal psychotherapy, guided self-help, group exercise. For SSRIs, a review is advised usually within 2 weeks, and after 1 week for people aged 18 to 25 or with particular concern about suicide risk.
